features.name: Formal academic attainment
features.description: This captures the level of formal academic training in computer science or a related field that the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree is stated, or the academic background is unclear.
A bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background is stated.
A master's degree in computer science or a related field is stated.
A doctoral degree in computer science or a related field is stated.

features.name: Relevant software tenure
features.description: This captures how much professional experience the applicant presents in software development work aligned to testing, maintaining, and launching products.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of relevant experience is shown, or the duration is unclear.
2 to 3 years of relevant software experience is shown.
4 to 5 years of relevant software experience is shown.
6 or more years of relevant software experience is shown.

features.name: Production delivery depth
features.description: This captures the extent of concrete production-service responsibility the letter describes across launch, maintenance, and operation.

levels.descriptor: No concrete production launches are described.
The letter shows work on 1 to 2 production services or gives only modest production evidence.
The letter shows repeated production delivery across 3 to 4 services.
The letter shows extensive production delivery across 5 or more services or clearly broad lifecycle ownership.

features.name: Go fluency signal
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter positions Go as a central professional language rather than a peripheral one.

levels.descriptor: Go is mentioned only briefly, or the depth of use is unclear.
Go is clearly used in professional work, but it is not framed as the applicant's main language.
Go is framed as a primary, daily, or chief working language in meaningful production context.

features.evidence: Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: Python fluency
features.description: This captures the depth and seriousness of the applicant's Python experience, especially for production systems and tooling.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned, or only incidental familiarity is implied.
Python is mentioned mainly for scripts or light tooling.
Python is presented as a regular language for services, automation, prototypes, or internal tools.
Python is presented as deeply production-ready, such as typed, tested, extensible, or broadly used across services and tooling.

features.evidence: shipping LLM-backed features and hardening them against unpredictable inputs
features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has moved beyond generic AI interest to deploying AI features responsibly in real systems.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned only as general interest, experimentation, or vague exposure.
The letter describes building or shipping AI or LLM features in production.
The letter describes production AI or LLM work together with evaluation, reliability, guardrails, or hardening practices.

features.evidence: Python agents that plan and execute bounded tasks
features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: This captures direct experience designing agent-based systems with explicit control boundaries and infrastructure around them.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or autonomous-tooling experience is mentioned.
Agents or automation are mentioned vaguely, with little architectural detail.
The letter shows clear experience building agent-based workflows or pipelines.
The letter gives a detailed agentic architecture, such as bounded actions, contracts, logging, auditing, permissions, or a clear Go and Python division of responsibility.

features.evidence: automated the intake and triage of vulnerability reports
features.name: Security workflow automation
features.description: This captures experience automating vulnerability handling or related security-response workflows to reduce manual effort.

levels.descriptor: No security automation example is provided.
The letter expresses interest in reducing security toil but does not claim ownership of such automation.
The letter shows a concrete example of automating vulnerability intake, triage, or handling.
The letter shows a concrete example with operational detail or impact, such as classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, self-serve flow, or time returned to experts.

features.evidence: threat models and code review for common vulnerability classes
features.name: Security assessment experience
features.description: This captures hands-on experience evaluating systems for security weaknesses and validating remediation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is described.
The letter shows general security interest but little concrete assessment practice.
The letter names concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, service review, or attack-surface analysis.
The letter shows strong assessment practice with attacker-minded reasoning, repeated ownership, or follow-through on remediation and validation.

features.evidence: turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation
features.name: Algorithmic problem solving
features.description: This captures whether the letter shows real use of data structures and algorithms to improve difficult engineering problems.

levels.descriptor: No data-structures or algorithms evidence is given.
The letter claims algorithmic strength but gives no concrete example.
The letter gives a concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or structure choice.
The letter gives a strong example on a hard or important problem that materially improved tractability, performance, or correctness.

features.evidence: near-top finishes in several large competitions
features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: This captures whether the applicant actively develops adversarial thinking through capture-the-flag work or similar offensive practice.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual CTF participation or similar practice.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows strong competitive results or especially serious, ongoing offensive-security practice.

features.name: Security credentialing
features.description: This captures the strength of external security validation the applicant cites.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
A foundational credential is mentioned, such as Security+.
An advanced hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP or stronger.

features.evidence: maintainer of an open-source tooling project
features.name: Open-source footprint
features.description: This captures the extent of public technical contribution or maintenance beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or bug fixes to dependencies.
The letter shows regular contributions or maintenance of a small public project or library.
The letter shows responsibility for a public project with outside users, contributors, reviews, releases, or clear maintainer ownership.

features.evidence: distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics
features.name: Personal systems building
features.description: This captures the ambition and technical rigor of self-directed projects described outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is described.
The letter describes a small utility or simple end-to-end app.
The letter describes a substantive side project with nontrivial backend, storage, or distributed-systems concerns.
The letter describes an ambitious system built from first principles or to production-like standards, especially around reliability, recovery, or fault tolerance.

features.name: Secure-defaults motivation
features.description: This captures how specifically the applicant connects their interest in the role to making security easier and more natural for developers.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows only generic interest in the company or title.
The letter shows general security interest but does not tie it to developer workflows or defaults.
The letter clearly connects the role to embedding security in the development lifecycle or reducing manual security toil.
The letter articulates a strong philosophy of secure defaults, proactive developer enablement, or higher engineering standards for security tooling.

features.evidence: improvements are inherited by everyone downstream
features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: This captures how well the letter understands and values the compounding impact of foundation-layer work across many teams.

levels.descriptor: No foundation-layer or cross-team impact motivation is shown.
The letter mentions scale or broad impact only in generic terms.
The letter explicitly values organization-wide leverage or foundation-layer impact.
The letter shows nuanced understanding of compounding leverage across teams or products, such as developer enablement at scale or fleet-wide protection.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned
features.name: Outcome specificity
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter supports its claims with owned examples and observable results.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on generic assertions with little supporting evidence.
The letter names some tasks or technologies but leaves ownership and outcomes vague.
The letter gives specific owned examples with clear practical effects.
The letter gives especially crisp evidence of impact, such as quantified results or vivid before-and-after operational change.

features.name: Proofreading quality
features.description: This captures the degree to which spelling, typing, and surface-level writing errors affect the letter's professionalism.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors materially distract from credibility and polish.
Several noticeable errors are present and weaken presentation.
The prose is mostly clean, with only minor slips.
The prose is clean and careful, with no distracting surface errors.

features.evidence: watching a minor dependency flaw ripple through an entire product line
features.name: Narrative framing
features.description: This captures whether the letter offers a memorable personal thesis or story rather than only listing fit statements.

levels.descriptor: The letter is a flat checklist or compliance-style restatement of qualifications.
The letter has competent motivation but remains mostly formulaic.
The letter presents a clear personal arc, viewpoint, or unifying theme.
The letter uses a memorable thesis, principle, or formative story that makes the application more distinctive and credible.
